gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured figure for any candidate. Techtest.org measured the LiTime 12V 100Ah Group24 Bluetooth at 102.46 Ah on average (100.92 Ah at 40 A) and the Power Queen 12V 100Ah Group 24 Smart at 104.26 Ah. Panbo found that the WattCycle 100Ah Bluetooth Group 24, whose BMS is rated 120 A, did not shut off until almost 200 A.
standout_why: I opened Nautworthy's LiTime Group 24 page (result 12 in the 2026-11-13 chat). It says Nautworthy has not tested the battery and gives only LiTime specs and its own sums. Solargenadvisor's trolling-motor page (in four chats) would not load because of a certificate error, so I could not check it. None of the six ChatGPT answers gives a measured capacity, cutoff voltage or trip current, and all of them rank on rated BMS amps. Our current page has only spec cells. I did not reopen the cited maker pages (Vatrer, Redodo, Power Queen, WattCycle). They are maker listings, so they cannot hold independent measurements.
decides: ChatGPT's main reason for picking Vatrer is that its 150 A BMS gives more headroom than everything else. No named reviewer has published a measurement for the Vatrer Group 24 150A, so that reason rests only on Vatrer's own claim. Panbo measured the WattCycle (rated 120 A) carrying almost 200 A before it shut off, so its real headroom is at least as big. Techtest measured more than 100 Ah from the LiTime and the Power Queen Group 24 at trolling-motor currents of 30 to 40 A. The page can say the headroom claim is unmeasured for Vatrer and measured for WattCycle. It can also say LiTime and Power Queen have verified capacity. Any of these covers a 55 lb motor drawing about 50 A. One practical catch comes from Panbo: the WattCycle stopped accepting charge at 14.2 V when charged at 25 A or more, so a 14.6 V LiFePO4 charger may cut out early.
